changes: Fixed: the floating audio play/pause bar (.audioBottomBar) could stay visible over the
Content Manager. Root cause: opening Manage never closes the article underneath it, it just
slides the CMS overlay on top — and the bar's z-index (120) is higher than the overlay's
(100), so a bar left showing from the article floated right over the CMS. Card-close itself
was already correct (closeArticle() already calls updateAudioBarPresence() after clearing
the open/peek/expanding classes) — this only affected the "still playing, then straight into
Manage" path.
Fix: updateAudioBarPresence() now also requires !manage.classList.contains('open'), and is
called at Manage's one open point (manageBtn click) and all three close points (Save & Exit,
its no-GitHub-token branch, and Discard). Single source of truth in the presence check itself,
so any future new way of opening/closing Manage stays correct without needing its own bar
call.
Ken Burns cycle sped up 16s -> 8s per Tom's "working but slow" feedback. Same ~9% scale/pan.
Added: Ken Burns drift on the article photo, Review Mode only (body.review-on class, synced
in setReviewMode() and on initial load from the stored review-mode preference). 16s,
ease-in-out, alternating, ~9% scale with a slight pan. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Root cause of v209-v212 doing nothing: the inline hero (.artimg / #artHeroImg) is not
the photo the reader sees. measureFly() sets hero.style.opacity = '0' and hands the picture
off to the body-level #flyPortrait copy, which is what is on screen at every scroll position.
Animating .artimg animated an invisible element. In v209/v210 it also scaled the exact rect
measureFly() reads to size and place the visible copy, which is what knocked the photo out of
its frame ("no longer centered with a border"). The animation now targets .flyPortrait img
instead - the container already has overflow:hidden and the img is object-fit:cover at
100%/100%, so the zoom is clipped by the badge's own gold frame and the frame never moves.
.flyPortrait's own scroll-driven transform is on the container, this is on the img inside it,
so the corner flight and the drift compose rather than fight.
Reverted the v211 .artimgWrap experiment (wrapper div around the hero img, #artHeroImgEl):
it was only there to clip an animation that no longer lives on that element, so the hero
markup and all its JS references are back to their pre-v209 shape. Net change from v208 is
the CSS block above plus the two body.review-on lines.
Debug: removed the body.review-on gate from the Ken Burns animation (temporarily
unconditional) to isolate why v211 showed no motion at all — border/centering was fixed by
v211, but that part isn't gated by review mode, so it never actually proved the gate was
working. If the photo now animates on ANY entry with a hero image (not just in Review Mode),
the gate/class wiring was the bug. If it still doesn't animate, the animation mechanism
itself is blocked by something else and the gate is unrelated.
Fixed: Ken Burns zoom was breaking out of the hero photo's border/centering — transform:
scale() on the bare grows the whole box, border included, with nothing to clip it.
Restructured: the hero is now a wrapper div (.artimgWrap, keeps id="artHeroImg", carries the
border/radius/margin/clip/overflow:hidden) around the actual (.artimg, new
id="artHeroImgEl", width:100%, no border of its own). Only the inner img animates; the
wrapper's frame stays fixed and clips the zoom, so the photo scales inside its border instead
of past it.
The two/three spots in JS that specifically need real load/.complete behavior
(restoreArticleScroll's apply(), jumpAndRevealSection's settle(), and the fly-portrait load
listener) now target #artHeroImgEl. Everything else that reads #artHeroImg (opacity toggles,
heroRestingRect(), measureFly()) keeps using the wrapper — which is actually more correct
than before, since it now reads a stable frame rect rather than one that could fluctuate
mid zoom-animation.
Temp: Ken Burns test sped way up (5s, 15% scale) and made obvious, purely to confirm the
effect fires at all — v209's 34s/7% version may simply have been too slow/subtle to notice
in a short glance. Revert to the slow version once confirmed working.
Added: Ken Burns test on the article hero image (.artimg) — slow (34s), subtle drift/zoom,
Review Mode only for now while it's being evaluated. Gated by a body.review-on class synced
in setReviewMode() and on initial load from the stored review-mode preference. Respects
prefers-reduced-motion. No changes to .flyPortrait or the hero-image fly/drag JS — the
animation targets .artimg's own transform only, so nothing that reads the hero's bounding
rect had to change.
Changed: 20 more years of scroll room on the timeline's left/B.C. side, per Tom's follow-up
(START -40 -> -60; the boundary tick now reads "60 BC"). Right side (END, 2070) unchanged.
No other code changes needed — v205's zone-math rewrite and the boundary tick's label already
read START generically rather than hardcoding the old value, so this was just the one constant
plus its synced ERAS entry (see the comment there for why that one can't just reference START
directly).
New: the bottom playback bar now also waits on a scroll-position gate, not just card state —
it fades in once Quick Facts (id="artFactBox", new) has scrolled up to within "an inch or two"
of the bottom of the screen (AUDIO_BAR_REVEAL_MARGIN, 130px), rather than appearing the instant
the card finishes opening while the reader's still looking at the hero photo.
This is a one-way latch (audioBarScrollRevealed), not a continuous show/hide tied to live
scroll position: once revealed, it stays revealed for the rest of that entry's viewing, even
scrolling back up past Quick Facts. Toggling right at the threshold line on every scroll tick
would be far more distracting than useful. Resets on every fresh openArticle() so each entry
re-earns its own reveal; does NOT reset on a peek<->full round-trip within the same entry.
checkAudioBarScrollReveal() is folded into the existing scroll-driven rAF loop (queueFly(),
already used for the flying photo) rather than given its own scroll listener — reusing that
established, debounced mechanism instead of adding a second one, partly on general principle
and partly because a new per-scroll-tick listener is exactly the shape of thing that caused
v205's jitter bug.
Entries with no Quick Facts at all (rare) skip the gate entirely — nothing to wait for.
Fix: the v205 bottom playback bar jittered as the article text scrolled. Root cause: it was
rendered inside #artBody's per-article HTML, nested inside #article — which is both the
scrolling container (overflow-y:auto) AND, deliberately, a transform-established containing
block for position:fixed descendants (see #article's own CSS comment). That combination is
exactly what this codebase's own #flyPortrait comment already warns about: a position:fixed
element nested inside a scrolling+transformed ancestor can end up visibly lagging/catching up
during active touch-scroll on iOS Safari, even though it lands in the technically-correct spot
the instant scrolling stops. #pauseIndicator gets away with this because it's invisible except
for a brief flash; a PERSISTENTLY VISIBLE bar makes the lag constant and obvious.
Fix: moved #audioBottomBar to a persistent body-level element, a sibling of #article next to
#flyPortrait (same fix that element already needed for a related reason), rather than
re-rendering it inside every article. Its three buttons are now wired exactly once — every
handler they call reads the current audioEl/currentCues at click time rather than closing over
anything from a particular render, so there was nothing to re-wire per article anyway. Needed
a z-index bump to match (120, matching #flyPortrait) since as a sibling it now has to out-rank
#article's own z-index:100 to render on top of the open card, rather than inheriting that for
free as a descendant.
Changed: updateAudioBarPresence() now also checks currentEntry.audio directly (the bar's mere
existence in the DOM no longer implies the open entry has audio, now that it's persistent
rather than conditionally rendered) — and initAudio() explicitly resets the button back to
Play on every entry open, since the element (and therefore its icon) now persists across
articles instead of starting fresh each time.
New: timeline range extended 40 years each direction (was AD 0-2030, now 40 BC-AD 2070) for
scroll room before Pentecost and after the current stretch. Found and fixed a real bug this
surfaced: yearToX/xToYear's 2x "widened Apostolic Age" zoom used to assume START and
DISTORT_START were the same year (both were 0) — extending START negative without separating
them would have silently pulled the whole B.C. padding into that 2x zone. Rewrote both as
proper 3-zone piecewise functions (undistorted / 2x / undistorted) so it doesn't.
New: a "B.C." era band and a labeled boundary tick (e.g. "40 BC") mark the new pre-Pentecost
stretch. fmtYear() and the new fmtAxisYear() both render negative years as "N BC".
Changed: the inline audio scrubber is gone, replaced by a fixed bottom bar (play/pause plus
jump-to-previous/next-SECTION, not seconds — see audJumpSection()/sectionBoundaryTimes(), which
read section boundaries straight from the timing file's cues rather than DOM matching, so
section-jumping works even on an entry whose sentence-highlighting is broken). No seek bar —
section jumping covers the navigation need a plain scrubber used to.
New: bottom-bar visibility follows the ARTICLE CARD's state, not playback state — visible any
time the entry has audio and the full card is up (not peeking, not mid slide/expand/collapse
transition), whether or not something is currently playing. Wired into all four card-state
transitions (openArticle, expandArticle, collapseArticle, closeArticle) via one shared check,
updateAudioBarPresence().
New: double-tap the story text to start/resume audio (outside Review Mode only — Review Mode's
own double-tap already means "select story for Speak Selection", so the two never compete for
the same gesture); a single tap anywhere in the story still stops it in place, as it already
did — now centralized through stopAudioPlaybackInPlace()/startAudioPlayback() so the bottom
bar's own button and both tap gestures share one code path. Added a fading play-triangle glyph
(showPlayIndicator()) as the double-tap's visual feedback, mirroring the existing pause glyph.
Removed: dead CSS/JS left over from the scrubber (.artPlayerWrap, .player, .pbtn, .ptime, the
old "tap anywhere on the scrubber row" handler) and the three occludedH calculations that used
to account for its sticky height — the bottom bar is fixed, not sticky-in-flow, so it no longer
occludes the top of the viewport at all. paintPlayerBackdrop() is left in place as a documented
no-op (same call as v196 made for wireSentenceCues' status line) rather than removed outright.
Added a bottom spacer (.audioBottomSpacer) to any entry with audio, so the fixed bar never
overlaps the last lines of the story or Sources & Further Reading.
Restored: the diagnostic sentence-sync status line under the scrubber ("Sentence sync: X/Y
sentences linked · Z section(s) mapped for follow-scroll"), removed in v196 once the sync bug
was believed fixed. It's back — gated to Review Mode + Owner Tools only (same gate as
triple-tap-to-link), so it never shows to a visitor. wireSentenceCues() itself was never
touched by the v196 removal (per that changelog note) — it was only ever the #apCueStatus DOM
element that was gone, so this is purely a template + CSS change, not a logic change. Useful
again now that the repair-cue-gaps.mjs batch tool is fixing older timing files in bulk: this
is the fastest way to confirm, per entry, that a given repair actually took.
Fix: v202 only stripped backslashes from the cue-text side of the comparison. Now the
article's own flattened search text (cueFlatMap()) drops any literal backslash character too
— never added to its flat string/DOM-offset map in the first place, so the two stay in
lockstep automatically, no separate cleanup pass needed. A stray backslash now breaks nothing
regardless of which side it turns up on — the article text, the cue text, or (per the
double-escaping bug this was chasing) both.
Changed: the highlighted-sentence indicator is no longer any change to the text itself
(color/weight from v198-v200 all reverted — .sentCue/.cuePlaying carry no visual styling now,
just the class toggle for JS to key off). Instead, a single glowing white bar (#audioActiveBar,
4px, layered box-shadow) sits flush against the actual left edge of the screen — a direct
child of #article itself rather than the narrower centered .artwrap column, so it always
touches the true edge regardless of screen width. Its top/height are set to span whichever
sentence is currently playing, computed in content-space (element position + current
scrollTop) so it scrolls naturally along with the article without needing to be re-positioned
every animation frame — same coordinate approach used throughout the follow-scroll features.
Hidden whenever there's no active cue, the entry has no audio, or the current sentence never
matched into the DOM.
Changed: highlighted-sentence style dropped the glow in favor of weight + brightness — every
matched sentence span (.sentCue) sits at a base ivory (#EEE8DC, matching the article's normal
parchment tone) at regular weight; the actively-playing one (.cuePlaying) goes pure white and
semi-bold (600), with both properties transitioning smoothly (150ms) as the highlight moves
from sentence to sentence.
Changed: highlighted-sentence style simplified to plain text color only — #F2CF72 (warm
gold), no left accent bar, no background, no text-shadow. Tried a left accent-bar variant
(position:absolute ::before with a glowing blue bar) per the owner's own CSS in this session,
but landed on text-color-only as the final choice.
Changed: the highlighted-sentence color switched from a cool silver (#E3E8F2) to a soft light
sky-blue (#AED8F0), color-matched from the owner's own reference screenshot — text color
only, no left-border accent bar (that bar belonged to a different, unrelated callout element
in the reference image, not something to carry over here).
New: a subtle dark text-shadow (0 1px 3px, 45% black) on the highlighted sentence, giving the
glyphs a touch of depth/pop against the page without any background tint or box-shadow.
New: within-section follow-scroll. Alongside the existing "ride to the top of a new section"
behavior, the actively-highlighted sentence is now kept fully on screen as playback moves
through a section that runs longer than one screenful — a smaller, more frequent nudge
(ensureActiveCueVisible()) than the section-level jump, triggered only when the current
section hasn't just changed. If the sentence fits with room to spare, its top lands just
below the sticky bars; if it's taller than the visible area even with margin, the view
favors bringing its bottom into view over its top, prioritizing what the reader hasn't heard
yet. Same manual-scroll deference as the rest of follow-along — never fights a reader
dragging the text themselves. followAudioSection() and the new function now share one small
orchestrator (driveAudioFollow()) that decides which of the two applies each tick.
Changed: the highlighted-sentence style dropped the gold background glow in favor of a plain
silver text color (#E3E8F2) — no background, no box-shadow, just the words themselves reading
a cooler, brighter tone against the page's warm parchment.
Removed: the small diagnostic status line under the scrubber ("X/Y sentences linked · Z
section(s) mapped…"), now that sentence-sync and follow-scroll are confirmed working. The
underlying status-reporting code in wireSentenceCues() is untouched and harmless — it just
looks up an element that no longer exists and no-ops — so it can come back with one line if a
future entry needs the same diagnosis again.
Fix: some of the missed sentence matches on St. John the Baptist (16/20) traced to
cross-reference links. Whenever a linked name (its first mention only, per the auto-link
convention — e.g. "Mary", "Jordan River", "Herod Antipas") is immediately followed by
punctuation in the source prose, generate-audio.mjs's tag-stripping leaves a stray space at
that boundary in the cue text ("Mary , newly pregnant") that the real rendered article never
has ("Mary, newly pregnant") — so the verbatim match failed for that whole sentence. Later
plain-text mentions of the same name (no link, since only the first mention gets one) never
carried the artifact, which is why it only hit some sentences. applyCueMarkup() now retries
an unmatched cue with a normalized version (a space directly before common punctuation
stripped) before giving up on it — fixes the mismatch without touching the generation script
or re-recording anything.
Changed: the section-follow glide (v191-v194) now rides to the top of a section every time
playback crosses into it, not only when that heading happens to already be off-screen — a
simpler, more literal "teleprompter" behavior: every new section always rises to the top.
Changed: audioTiming is no longer a separate field to set on every entry. The timing path is
now derived automatically from the audio path — same folder, same base name, just `.json`
instead of `.mp3`/`.wav` (e.g. audio/Saints/x-v1.mp3 → audio/Saints/x-v1.json), matching the
actual convention generate-audio.mjs already outputs to. A new sync file just has to exist
alongside its audio to start working; no patch, no field to remember. An explicit
`audioTiming` value, if ever set on an entry, still wins over the derived guess — an escape
hatch for the rare case where the timing file doesn't follow the convention.
The status line's wording adjusted to match: a derived-but-missing timing file (the normal
state for any entry whose audio hasn't been through the sync step yet) now reads "no timing
file yet" rather than the old "no audioTiming linked to this entry," since there's no longer
a link to set in the first place.
Confirmed against a real audioTiming file (st-john-the-baptist-30-v1.json): the cue schema
does carry `type:"heading"`, exactly what computeCueSectionHeadings() (v192) already checks
for first. So the matching logic itself isn't the failure — the status line not appearing at
all was the real clue: that line only renders when `d.audioTiming` is truthy, so its total
absence (not just an unhelpful message) means the entry being tested most likely doesn't have
an audioTiming path set yet, even if the timing file itself exists and audio is playing fine.
Fix: the status line now renders for any entry with audio at all, not only ones with
audioTiming linked — and reports plainly ("no audioTiming linked to this entry") when that's
the case, instead of the whole line just not existing. A missing link and a genuine blank are
no longer visually identical.
Fix: wireSentenceCues() now wraps the cue-matching + section-mapping step in its own
try/catch and reports any real error as visible status text ("Sentence sync error: …")
instead of letting an exception vanish into a silently-rejected async function with no
visible trace.
Fix: follow-along auto-scroll (v191) never triggered — reported as "the text just sits there
through the whole playing article." Root cause: cueSectionHeading was built by looking for
[data-cue-idx] elements in the DOM, which only exist where a cue's SENTENCE successfully
matched into #artStoryText's actual text (applyCueMarkup) — a separate, more fragile
verbatim-text match that silently breaks the moment an entry's prose is edited after its
audio was generated. If that per-sentence matching comes up empty (which looks likely to be
happening on the entries tested — see the highlighting complaint from before this feature was
even built), cueSectionHeading ended up entirely empty too, so every single follow check
bailed out immediately with nothing to go on. computeCueSectionHeadings() no longer depends
on that at all: it now walks currentCues directly against the DOM's actual .arth headings (in
order), recognizing a heading cue either by the timing file's own `type:"heading"` flag or,
as a fallback, by its text matching the next expected heading exactly — neither of which
requires ordinary sentence cues to have matched anything.
New: the small status line under the scrubber (visible on any entry with audioTiming) now
also reports how many sections it mapped for follow-scroll, alongside the existing
sentence-linked count — e.g. "12/40 sentences linked · 6 section(s) mapped for
follow-scroll" — so it's visible at a glance whether each half of the sync is actually
working, without needing dev tools.
New: follow-along auto-scroll during audio playback. While the narration plays, whenever the
highlighted sentence moves into a section whose heading isn't on screen, the view eases up
or down (same decelerating glide as the resume-reveal feature, clearing the sticky header
and audio scrubber the same way) to bring that section's heading into view — so the text
being read stays visible without the reader having to touch anything. Also fires the instant
Play is pressed, not just on section changes: scroll to the bottom of a long entry, hit Play
from the start, and the view jumps straight to wherever playback is actually beginning.
Tapping a sentence to seek (existing feature) benefits too, though it's usually a no-op there
since the tapped sentence is already visible.
A genuine manual scroll (touchmove or wheel — not just a tap, so pressing Play/seek/a cue
itself never counts) silences the follow-along for 4 seconds and immediately stops any
follow animation already in progress, so it never fights a reader repositioning the text
themselves. It re-arms automatically once that window passes.
New: cueSectionHeading — built once per entry right after cues are matched, mapping each
matched cue to the section heading that governs it (walked directly off the rendered DOM, not
the timing file's own section numbers, for the same reliability reason documented above
applyCueMarkup).
Fix: on entries with audio, the section-reveal glide (v187-v189) still landed the heading
underneath the audio scrubber. Cause: the scrubber (#artPlayerWrap) is ALSO sticky — it pins
itself directly beneath the sticky header once scrolled past, per its own CSS
(top:var(--ahH)) — so on any entry with audio there are two bars stacked at the top of the
viewport, not one, and the reveal math only ever accounted for the header's height. It now
adds the scrubber's own height too (only when the entry actually has one) to both the
section-membership check and the reveal target, so the heading clears both bars — audio
entries and silent entries land in the same visually-correct spot now.
Fix: reopening the same card repeatedly crept one section further back each time. Cause:
the section-reveal math (v187/v188) compared the raw scroll position against each heading's
raw offset to decide which section "governs" the landing spot — but after a reveal glide
lands the reader with the heading sitting just below the sticky header (by design), that
heading's true offset is now a few pixels past the raw scroll position, so the very next
reopen's comparison wrongly credited the section BEFORE it and eased up again — and again on
the next reopen after that. The comparison now accounts for the sticky header's own height
(the actual visible reading position is scrollTop + header height, not raw scrollTop) with
matching slack on both the "which section" check and the reveal-target math, so a
properly-revealed heading is recognized as already current and reopening the same spot
twice in a row is a no-op the second time, not another step backward.
Fix: v187's "ease back up to the section heading" reveal was scrolling to the heading's raw
offset, which put it directly underneath the card's own sticky header (#artSticky, pinned to
the top of the visible area) — so the title never actually became visible. The reveal target
now backs off further: sticky-header-height-plus-a-little-breathing-room past the heading's
top, so the title actually clears the sticky bar and is genuinely on screen once the glide
finishes, not just technically scrolled past.
Changed: reopening a card at a remembered position (v184/v185/v186) no longer glides down
from the top of the card at all — that read as distracting regardless of speed. It now
jumps straight to the saved scroll position instantly, exactly like the audio and the
hero-photo-position restore already did. The only motion left is orienting, not
"here's-a-neat-effect": if the landing spot is more than a hair into its section (not
already sitting right at that section's heading), the view eases gently back up — a short,
slow, purely upward glide — to reveal that section's title, giving the reader a beat to
place themselves before continuing. A spot that already lands right at a section's top
skips that step entirely, since there's nothing to reveal.
Changed: the resume-scroll glide from v185 slowed way down (900ms → 2.2s) — it was reading
as an instant jump, not a deliberate glide.
Removed: the paragraph glow/dim pulse that fired when the resume glide landed. Owner found
it looked odd rather than helpful — the slower glide itself is now what signals "here's
where you were," with nothing highlighted at the end.
New: reopening a card at a remembered position (via icon tap or swipe to a neighbor — see
v184) now rides there instead of teleporting. The card opens at the top as always, then
scrolls smoothly down to the saved spot over about 0.9s with a decelerating ease-out (fast
start, gentle landing), and the single paragraph it lands on gets one soft gold glow-and-dim
pulse — same gold as the audio sentence-highlight — so it's visually obvious the app found
the actual place, not just that the page happens to be scrolled somewhere. The Back button's
own restore (undoing an in-article cross-reference tap) is deliberately left as an instant
jump, unchanged — that's a quick "undo," not a "welcome back" moment.
Fix (the real gap): reopening a card via the normal route — tapping its icon on the
timeline — always calls showDetail(), which asks openArticle() for the teaser peek
(opts.peek:true). v182/v183's recent-position lookup explicitly skipped that path
("&& !opts.peek"), so a saved scroll position was found and then thrown away every time,
and the reader always landed back on the plain teaser no matter how recently they'd been
reading. The lookup now runs BEFORE the peek/full decision: if there's a real, unexpired
(within the hour) mid-article position on file, it wins outright — opts.peek is forced
false and the reader goes straight back into the full story at that scroll position,
which is what "remembering where you were" was always supposed to mean. A fresh card with
no recent position still opens to the normal teaser, unchanged.
Fix: the same gap existed on left/right swipe between chronological neighbors —
slideArticleTo() restored a recent audio position but never scroll, always resetting to
the top of the incoming entry regardless of how recently it had been read. It now restores
scroll the same way openArticle() does.
Fix (the actual point of v182): collapseArticle() — the step a swipe-down normally takes
BEFORE fully closing, full story down to the peek preview — was resetting article.scrollTop
to 0 as part of that animation, with nothing capturing the real reading position first. So
the very moment a reader swiped down (even just once, accidentally, without meaning to
close anything), their place was already gone by the time closeArticle() ran and tried to
save it — v182's whole recently-viewed-cards mechanism was saving a scroll of 0 for exactly
the accidental-swipe case it was built to protect against. Now collapseArticle() saves the
card's real position the instant it's invoked, before touching scrollTop, so a reader who
swipes away — on purpose or by accident — always gets their actual place back within the
hour, not just the top of the card.
Fix (the real one this time, probably): syncAudioStatusFromGitHub() fetches data.json from the
live SITE, not straight from GitHub's API — which means it's actually reading whatever
Cloudflare has deployed, and a push takes real time (seconds to roughly a minute) to actually
redeploy. Every previous version of this sync blindly did `e.audio = f.audio` regardless of
whether `f.audio` was populated, so a sync that raced Cloudflare's deploy lag — which the panel-
open toggle listener risked on literally every use — would silently WIPE an already-good
audio/audioTiming field back to blank/undefined from a stale pre-deploy snapshot. This is almost
certainly why sentence-highlighting "worked for a while, then stopped" on entries recorded well
before this session, and why a freshly-recorded entry's link kept failing to appear even on a
confirmed-latest build: the very act of opening the Record Audio panel to check could erase the
thing being checked for. The merge is now non-destructive — `if(f.audio) e.audio = f.audio`,
same for audioTiming — so a sync that races the deploy is a harmless no-op instead of active
data loss.
New: syncAudioStatusUntilFresh() — since a non-destructive sync can still legitimately just not
see the new field yet if it runs too soon, the Record button's post-completion handler now
polls up to 8 times (8s apart) until every entry it just requested actually shows a real `audio`
value, updating the log with "waiting for the site to finish deploying…" in between rather than
trying once and quietly giving up.
Caveat: this only prevents future data loss. If an entry's audioTiming was already wiped to
blank in a past session and that state got published to GitHub, the field is genuinely gone
from data.json and needs the entry re-recorded (Overwrite checked) rather than just re-synced.
Increased the play/pause button's touch target (66px → 76px, explicit min-width/min-height,
touch-action:manipulation) and set pointer-events:none on its SVG icons so a tap anywhere in
the button's circle always reaches the <button> itself rather than depending on hitting the
icon's own painted pixels.
Fix: confirmed via a real recording (St. James the Greater, generate-audio.yml reported
success in 78s, file genuinely landed at audio/Saints/st-james-greater-44-v1.mp3) that
syncAudioStatusFromGitHub() (v178/v179) was in fact updating db.entries correctly all along —
the bug was one level up. The Entries editor's #fAudio field is a plain <input> that
openEditor() fills in once, at the moment an entry is opened; nothing re-populated it when
db.entries changed out from under it afterward, so an editor left open across a recording (or
reopened right after one) kept showing the field empty/stale even though the real data was
fine. syncAudioStatusFromGitHub() now re-runs openEditor(editingId) whenever the entry
currently open in the editor is one of the ones it just synced, so the visible form updates
immediately rather than needing to be closed and reopened by hand.
Fix: v178 only auto-synced audio/audioTiming when the Record Audio panel was opened or right
before a dispatch — never after a run actually finished, so the result of every recording still
needed a manual reopen (or full app reload) to become visible/playable. The Record button's
click handler now chains onto triggerWorkflow()'s own promise (it already awaits the run's
completion via polling) and calls syncAudioStatusFromGitHub() the moment that resolves, whether
the run succeeded, failed, or the poll simply gave up after ~60s. Since that sync mutates the
same db.entries objects the rest of the app reads from, an entry's article — even one already
open in this session — picks up its new audio without needing to be reopened.
Caveat worth knowing: this only covers runs the button's own poll actually observed finish
(typically well within its ~60s window for a 1-5 entry batch, per this app's own run-time
history). An unusually long batch that outlasts the poll will still need the panel reopened
once — which itself re-syncs (v178) — to pick up the result.
New: syncAudioStatusFromGitHub() — refreshes just the `audio`/`audioTiming` fields on the
in-memory entries from the live data.json (same cache-busted fetch pattern as boot-time
loadDb()) before the Record Audio pool is computed. Fires twice: once when the "Record Audio
Narration" panel is opened (via a `toggle` listener on the new #audioRecordDetails id), and
again right before the actual dispatch inside the button's own click handler — since the panel
may have sat open for a while and another run could have finished narrating entries in the
meantime. Deliberately merges only those two fields per entry rather than replacing the whole
db, so any unsaved edits elsewhere in the session are untouched. This closes the gap that let a
"start at Michael, record 3" batch try an entry the session's own (stale) copy of db didn't yet
know had already been narrated.
The Start Year label and batch-preview list both show "Checking latest narration status…"
while this sync is in flight, so it's visible rather than a silent pause.
Fix: the Record Audio Narration card had no category filter at all — audioCandidatePool()
pulled from every entry type sorted purely by year, so a "Start at St. Michael, record 3"
request could (and did) walk straight past two Saints and pick up a Council or a different
Marian entry just because their years happened to fall in between. Added a Category dropdown
(All categories, or one of Saint/Council/Persecution/Marian Apparition/Eucharistic
Miracle/Event); audioCandidatePool() now filters on it, so the Start Year navigator only steps
through that one category and the resulting batch is genuinely locked to it. Category is sent
as the `category` workflow_dispatch input when no explicit start entry is chosen, and implicitly
enforced via the `ids` list when one is (since the pool itself is already filtered).
Category is remembered per-device alongside the rest of the card's settings (added to
AUDIO_GEN_FIELDS). Changing it resets the Start Year position back to "earliest in this
category" rather than keeping a numeric index that pointed at the wrong entry under the old
category's pool.
Fix: sentence-highlighting/tap-to-seek (v171) matched almost nothing on real narrated
entries. Root cause: generate-audio.mjs computes each cue's `section` number against its own
internal, FILTERED list of sections (sectionParts() drops any section with empty body before
numbering them), while the app's old applyCueMarkup() grouped cues by that same number against
the *unfiltered* list of rendered .arth/.artProse pairs — so on any entry with even one
empty-bodied section, every cue after it pointed at the wrong section and silently failed to
match. Fixed by dropping section-based grouping entirely: applyCueMarkup() now builds one flat
text map of the whole #artStoryText container and matches cues sequentially by verbatim text
alone, the same way sentences within a section already worked — `section` numbers are no
longer read at all. cueSectionElements() (now unused) removed.
New: the Record Audio Narration card (v172) gets a start-year navigator instead of always
recording from the earliest entry needing audio. Type a year to jump near it, then ←/→
to land on the exact entry to begin from. audioCandidatePool() mirrors generate-audio.mjs's
own candidateEntries() default (chronological, has narratable text via the existing
articleStats().wordCount, has/lacks audio per the Overwrite checkbox) so the entry shown is
always exactly what a blank-ids run would have picked at that position — arrowing just moves
the starting point within it. audioStartIdx stays -1 (no explicit start) until a year is
entered or an arrow is pressed; toggling Overwrite re-renders the preview since it changes
pool membership.
On Record: if a start entry is chosen, the next `count` ids from that point in the pool are
sent as an explicit `ids` input, overriding the script's own blank-ids/category auto-select.
No start chosen — ids/category stay blank, unchanged from v172's behavior.
Start year resets (and the field clears) each time Manage is opened, so a stale starting point
from an earlier session never silently carries into a new one.
New: Manage → Import → "Record Audio Narration" card. Triggers the existing generate-audio.yml
Action directly from the app (reusing the same triggerWorkflow()/run-and-poll machinery as
Resize Images / Convert Photo PNGs, now extended to accept a workflow_dispatch `inputs` object
instead of always sending a bare {ref}). Fields: Voice ID, how many to record, and a collapsed
"Voice & pacing settings" section (model, speed, stability, similarity boost, style, speaker
boost, heading/section pause, narrate-headings toggle, overwrite toggle). ids/category are left
blank on the dispatch — generate-audio.mjs's own candidateEntries() already sorts the whole
catalog chronologically and skips anything with existing audio, so "record the next N" is just
its default no-ids/no-category path; Overwrite maps straight to its own input.
New: every field on that card is remembered per-device in localStorage
('audio-gen-settings', saved at record-time) and reloaded whenever Manage opens
(prefillAudioGen(), alongside the existing prefillGh()/prefillAssetBase() calls) — so voice ID
and tuning only have to be set once. First run on a device with nothing saved yet prefills
Voice ID with the project's current voice.
Fix: v169's double-tap-to-select-story did nothing on iPhone. Cause: #artStoryText had no
touch-action set, so iOS Safari's native double-tap-to-zoom gesture consumed the double-tap

#artStoryText{touch-action:manipulation;} alongside the existing .artSticky touch-action
rule. No JS changes.

window.getSelection()/document.createRange(), called at the end of fillArticleBody only

Off entirely outside Review Mode — no behavior change for visitors. Note for the owner: the

which turns a real newline into
for display — this just makes that reachable from the

Icon jitter, round 2 (diagnosed from a second screen recording): moving the icon's position to
JS (done in v137/v140 to fix the touching-the-next-band bug) traded one problem for another —
JS position only updates on 'scroll' events, which iOS coalesces to well under 60fps during a

Position is back to native CSS position:sticky (compositor-driven, perfectly smooth, matches

Found the actual cause of the "too much coffee" jittery/flickering band icons (diagnosed from
a screen recording, frame-by-frame): an existing window 'resize' handler ran a full render()
(wipes and rebuilds the entire canvas) on every resize event, and iOS Safari fires 'resize'
repeatedly during ordinary scrolling as its address-bar toolbar shows/hides — not just on real
rotations. That caused the whole timeline, icons included, to briefly blank out and rebuild
mid-scroll. The resize handler is now debounced (220ms) so rapid-fire scroll-driven resizes
collapse into a single render once things settle; real resizes/rotations still work.
Also dropped the CSS opacity transition on the band icon — it was fighting the JS-driven
per-scroll-frame opacity updates (chasing a constantly-moving target), adding a second,

Picks the most prominent (lowest-tier) saint if more than one shares the day. Silently does
nothing if no saint's feast falls on today or if facts/Feast day data is missing/unparsable.
Apostolic Age's 25/50/75 tick labels now match the full century-mark styling (bright gold,
13px) instead of the dimmer/smaller "minor" tick style — they were being treated as lesser
ticks even though they're this zoomed-in era's equivalent of a century mark.
Era band font size up another notch (11.5px → 12.5px), letter-spacing eased slightly further.
Closing an article now leaves a clue on the timeline: the icon you were just reading lights up
(the same gold glow search uses for a match) and the timeline recentres on it, instead of
dropping you back with no trace of where you'd been.
Left/right swipe between chronological neighbors now shares the same back-stack as following
an in-article link — Back can undo a swipe too, landing you back at the same scroll position.
A swipe that lands exactly back where a previous swipe came from pops that frame instead of
pushing a new one, so casual back-and-forth swiping doesn't grow the stack without bound.
Era band font size up a notch (10.5px → 11.5px), letter-spacing eased slightly to compensate.
Hamburger menu reordered: "Make this into an App" (with its expand-to-see install steps) now
sits first, above Font Size — previously it was lower in the list. Combined with the panel
moving higher (top offset 84px → 58px, more usable height), those steps now sit near the top
of the screen instead of getting hidden behind iOS's own share sheet when you actually follow
them.
Added a 4th install step: "Press the circle in the bottom right," after Tom found the
3-step version left one step out on his device.
New: update-available glow. The hamburger pulses gold a few times, once, the first time a
newer version is detected — queued for the moment the panel is next closed, since the icon is
hidden while the panel is open. The "New Version Available" row itself gets the same brief
glow the next time the panel is opened. Neither glows continuously; each fires once per newly
seen version.
Added "Test Update Glow" under Owner Tools — previews both glows on demand (fake "vTEST"
label, auto-reverts after 16s) without needing an actual version mismatch to test against.
Era band (the "Apostolic Age" / "Age of Martyrs" row) redone as one continuous gold
surface — a top-to-bottom highlight/shadow gradient that looks like a single curved
gold bar running the whole width, rather than each era being its own alternating gold
tint. Text is now bold dark navy for contrast. A dark divider line (not a color change)
now marks where one era ends and the next begins.
heroLogo nudged right (right:30px, was 46px) — it was overlapping the "v120" version stamp next to the title on a live screenshot.

heroLogo's fade reworked again: it's now driven directly by how close the article's flying photo actually is to heroLogo's own corner — 0 while it's elsewhere (peek, top of a freshly-opened article, closed), fading toward fully hidden only as the scroll-driven corner badge settles into that exact spot, and back the moment it leaves (article closes, collapses to peek, or the reader scrolls back up). The previous version faded it for a fixed ~220ms window and then always brought it back regardless of whether the badge was still sitting there — this fixes that: as long as the badge occupies the corner, the graphic now stays faded, with no timer to time out.
The fade transition slowed from .3s to 1.2s so it reads as a gradual dissolve rather than a noticeable pop, in both directions.

heroLogo image regenerated without the central-width crop that was cutting off both flanking cupolas — only the dead space above the cross is trimmed now, so the full dome (both side towers included) is visible, matching the owner's reference goal image.
Resized to 150×130px (was 56×74px) to suit the now-wider, uncropped aspect ratio, with the small-screen breakpoint scaled proportionally.

heroLogo shrunk to fit entirely within the header (56×74px, was 122×160px) — it was spilling past the header into the era-band row and crowding the "Age of Martyrs" label on a live screenshot. No new cropping of the source image; this is a pure CSS resize.

heroLogo's fade behavior reworked per owner feedback: it no longer fades just because a peek card or full article is open. It now only fades while the article's flying photo is actually moving through #heroLogo's own top-right corner — the scroll-driven shrink into the corner badge, and the collapse-to-peek flight (not the expand-away-from-the-corner flight, which is leaving that spot, not crossing it). A short idle debounce (220ms) brings it back once the photo has settled rather than the instant a single animation frame ends.
Header graphic replaced with a new dome-and-cross image, re-cropped to trim the dead space above the cross so it sits closer to the image's own top edge.

heroLogo repositioned: shifted up (top:-8px) and further left (right:44px, was right:8px) to give the hamburger menu clear breathing room, per the live-screenshot check showing the two crowding each other.

Header's top background color changed from #0A1430 to #030B20 — sampled directly from the new image's own corner/edge pixels — so the graphic's rectangular edge blends into the page instead of showing a visible seam.
Timeline search box narrowed from 320px to 224px (about 70% of its former width) and its text enlarged, staying above the 16px floor that keeps iOS Safari from auto-zooming on focus.

New fixed header graphic (Images/heroLogo.png, a cropped dome-and-cross image) fills the gap the narrower search box opened up next to the hamburger menu, reaching from the top of the screen down through the header and controls bar to the edge of the timeline. Edges are softened with a CSS mask rather than a hard rectangle. It is decorative and non-interactive (pointer-events:none) so it never blocks taps on the hamburger, search box, or timeline pins.
The graphic fades out via body.artOpen whenever a card (peek) or full article opens, so it never competes with open content — the same convention the earlier, since-removed monstrance graphic used.

Wired up the true installable-PWA icon path that was already scaffolded in the file: the APP_ICON constant now points at real hosted icon files (Images/icons/apple-touch-icon.png, icon-192.png, icon-512.png) instead of null, so Add to Home Screen picks up the new gold-domed cross artwork instead of the old embedded placeholder.
Runtime web manifest's background_color changed to a gold/cream tone to match the new icon's launch/splash feel; theme_color and app name unchanged.
No changes to the timeline, article view, or Content Manager in this build.

Content Manager fully reskinned to match the app's own Settings sheet throughout, not just the Logs tab: sans-serif system font, larger text, and flat white rows on a light gray page background in place of the gold-tinted, Cinzel/EB Garamond serif card look used everywhere else in the CMS (Entries, Export, Import, Settings, the exit-confirmation dialog).

The tab menu moved from a scrolling row under the header to a fixed bottom tab bar — icon over label, five equal-width thumb-reachable targets, matching standard iOS tab-bar placement. The Content Manager top bar now holds only the title and Exit.
The public-facing timeline and article view are untouched — this redesign is scoped entirely to the owner-only Content Manager chrome.
Logs tab: dates now display as "Monday 8/8  12:45 PM" instead of the raw ISO timestamp.

The button beside search now reads "Search" and explicitly re-runs the filter, instead of "Refresh" (data still reloads automatically every time the Logs tab is opened, so nothing was lost by dropping the separate refresh action).
Search matches are now highlighted in yellow across version, date, and change text.

Redesigned the Logs tab to mimic the app's own Settings sheet rather than the rest of the Content Manager's serif/gold theme: sans-serif system font throughout, larger text, and flat full-height rows in place of the small boxed card. Change lists are now numbered (1, 2, 3…) instead of bulleted. The panel now cancels the surrounding padding so it runs edge-to-edge and fills the remaining screen height.

Replaced the header's gear/hamburger icon (was the ⚙/☰ unicode characters, which iOS renders as a glossy 3D emoji-style glyph) with a flat, simple, single-color SVG gear/lines icon that follows the site's gold color exactly.

Fixed the gear icon overlapping the Content Manager's Exit button: the gear sits at a fixed top-right position with a high z-index (so it stays reachable from any screen, including Manage), which the new sticky Content Manager header didn't leave room for. The header now reserves space on the right for it, and Exit is wider with more breathing room.

Content Manager header simplified: Exit button now just reads "Exit" instead of "Exit Content Manager", and the version badge now matches the "Content Manager" title's font (Cinzel) instead of a different serif.
